issue.title: Define fail-closed recovery when protected-state logout resets fail
issue.body:
Follow-up to the logout-sweep review on #243. The backend-field compatibility fix now attempts the remaining protected states after a reset failure, logs the failed state's name, and re-raises the first error after the sweep. Factory output is no longer deep-copied.

Recovery inside a failed state needs a separate auth-lifecycle change. Simply swallowing field or state exceptions and returning success can leave the previous user's protected data accessible on the same client token.

Follow-up work:

- Define a fail-closed session invalidation/recovery policy when a protected default factory, setter, or state load fails during logout.
- Decide whether to continue clearing other fields and computed caches within the failed state, while retaining a failure signal.
- Cover subsequent login on the same token so protected data left in a failed state cannot reach the next user.
- Cover provider cleanup and browser cookie synchronization when application cleanup fails.

The existing `get_state` failure handling and per-field recovery are deliberately unchanged in #243 to keep the backend API migration focused.
